comments.author: dahart
comments.story_title: For modern development, Javascript is just something you need to learn
comments.why_zh: 改变怀疑者对 JavaScript 的看法；展示其类似 Lisp 的根源和命名历史。
comments.quote_zh: 这个视频改变了我的想法
comments.text_zh: 我承认自己曾经是个反 JavaScript 的精英主义者（其实并不真正了解 JS）。这个视频改变了我的想法：[VIDEO]（Google Tech Talk，《JavaScript: The Good Parts》）视频里提到两个我以前不知道、并让我对 JavaScript 感觉更好的事实：1- JavaScript 是伪装的 Lisp 2- JavaScript 这个名字是个内部笑话，指的是这门语言与 Java 的不同之处，而不是相似之处。这就足以让我改变想法，我现在正毫无羞愧地享受着学习 JavaScript。浏览器差异和缺乏标准很让人头疼（PITA），但另一方面，它们都有很棒的调试器——HTML+JavaScript 可能是唯一随所有电脑预装的 UI 工具包 + 开发环境，因此触达面最广。毫无疑问，与其他语言相比，JS 世界有点像蛮荒西部，但也毫无疑问，情况正在随着时间变好，而且取决于你在写什么，使用它有很大优势。
comments.text: I will admit to having been an anti-JavaScript elitist (without really knowing JS.) This video changed my mind: [VIDEO] (google tech talk, "JavaScript: the good parts") Two facts mentioned in the video that I didn't previously know and make me feel better about JavaScript: 1- JavaScript is lisp in disguise 2- The name JavaScript is an inside joke referencing the language's differences from Java, not its similarities. That was enough to make me change my mind, and I'm currently enjoying learning JavaScript unashamedly. Browser differences and lack of standards are a PITA, but OTOH, they all have awesome debuggers - HTML+JavaScript may be the only UI toolkit + dev environment that comes packaged with ALL computers, and for that reason has the widest reach. There's no question that the JS world is a bit wild west compared to other languages, but there's also no question that the situation is getting better over time, and that depending on what you're coding, there are huge advantages to using it.

comments.author: just2n
comments.story_title: Learning JavaScript - my experience and advice
comments.text_zh: TGP 大多是教条。书名本应把这一点说得非常清楚，但不幸的是，和往常一样，Crockford 目光短浅，所以他这本书的标题具有误导性，暗示你读它就能学到一些关于这门语言的东西。更合适的标题应该是 “JavaScript: Crockford's Best Practices for Experienced JavaScripters”，或者 “What's Wrong With JavaScript According to Crockford”。这样就能很清楚地看出这本书在做什么，也不会诱使读者以为它是一本入门或学习书。Crockford 的少数观点被相当广泛地接受为良好建议，但其中大部分往好了说也是有争议的，在实践中则是不正确或误导性的。如果你正考虑买它，不如直接看那场演讲：[VIDEO] 。至于那篇文章：大部分建议都很合理。我要再次强调读源码，以此强调并作为支撑。我最近开始向那些对这门语言已经比较熟悉的人推荐这样做。这些代码库里用到许多流行的模式和技术，而且从阅读角度看非常平易近人。几个月前我把这两个都读了，为了熟悉一个新项目；相比读 jQuery 或 Angular 这类东西，我觉得相当享受。
comments.text: TGP is mostly dogma. The title should make that very clear, but unfortunately, as usual, Crockford is short sighted so the title of his book is misleading, implying you might learn something about the language by reading it. A much more appropriate title would've been "JavaScript: Crockford's Best Practices for Experienced JavaScripters", or "What's Wrong With JavaScript According to Crockford." Then it's pretty clear what the book is doing, and doesn't trick readers into thinking it's an introductory or learning book. A few of Crockford's opinions are fairly widely accepted as good advice, but much of it is controversial at best, and in practice incorrect or misguided. If you are considering buying it, just watch the talk instead: [VIDEO] . As for the article: it's mostly sound advice. I will reiterate reading the source to underscore and backbone. I started recommending this lately to people after they get comfortable with the language. Many popular patterns and techniques are used in these code bases and they're very approachable from a reading perspective. I read both a few months ago to get up to speed on a new project and I found it quite enjoyable compared to reading the likes of jQuery or Angular.
